name: Bitstamp Public Market Data API
summary: Keyless public market data from the Bitstamp exchange: tickers, OHLC candles back to 2011, order books, recent trades, currencies and trading pairs.
description: Bitstamp's v2 REST API serves public market data without authentication: per-market tickers, all-market tickers, hourly tickers, order books, recent transactions, OHLC candles at granularities from 1 minute to 3 days, plus currency and trading-pair listings. It is the source behind the widely used Kaggle 'Bitcoin Historical Data' minute-level OHLC dataset. Private trading endpoints require signed keys and are not covered here.

auth.notes: Public data functions answered without credentials; private endpoints need API keys with signed requests.

rate_limit.summary: Documented: 400 requests per second by default, and a default threshold of 10,000 requests per 10 minutes; exceeding it returns error 400.002.

endpoints.summary: Latest price, 24h open/high/low, volume, bid and ask
OHLC candles; step in seconds, limit 1 to 1000
All trading pairs and their rules
Currencies with supply and network details

license.name: Bitstamp terms (terms page is behind a bot wall; not read)

coverage.geographic: Global crypto and fiat pairs listed on Bitstamp
coverage.temporal: Live data; BTC/USD candles queried from start=1325376000 (January 2012) returned data

agent_notes: Market symbols are lower-case base+quote without a separator, for example btcusd. Numbers come back as strings. OHLC needs step (seconds) and limit (1 to 1000); use start with a unix timestamp to page through history, since there is no cursor. The 1-minute candle for early 2012 exists but often has zero volume. For streaming use the documented websocket API instead of polling.
caveats: CORS was inconsistent: /ohlc/ and /currencies/ sent Access-Control-Allow-Origin * while /ticker/ sent no CORS header.
The site sits behind Imperva; the terms-of-use page returned a bot-wall stub, so licence and reuse terms were not confirmed.
The API docs page embeds an OpenAPI document but no spec URL was found, so none is linked.
limit above 1000 on /ohlc/ returns a validation error.

verification.notes: Example executed without credentials (200, about 0.15 s); ticker, order_book, transactions, trading-pairs-info and currencies also returned 200. A missing and a curl-default User-Agent both worked.
